codebook_metadata.title: Existential Analysis & Logotherapy Four Fundamental Motivations (4FMs) Codebook - Version 5.0 (Omni-Merge)
codebook_metadata.purpose: Comprehensive interpretive thematic analysis framework for understanding participant experiences in therapeutic interventions using the Four Fundamental Motivations (4FMs) of Existential Analysis and Logotherapy.
codebook_metadata.methodology: Integrative synthesis of parallel-developed codebook versions (Claude v4.0, ChatPGT5 v4.0, Gemini v4.0), combining theoretical depth, clinical correlation, and practical coding granularity.
codebook_metadata.theoretical_foundation: Four Fundamental Motivations of Existential Analysis (Längle)

merged_from_versions.ChatPGT5_v4.0: Practical coding structure, detailed sub-themes (STs), granular inclusion/exclusion criteria, direct source quotes.
merged_from_versions.Claude_v4.0: Comprehensive theoretical foundation, existential core concepts, and detailed metadata/version history.
merged_from_versions.Gemini_v4.0: Clear high-level FM summaries, clinical/pathology correlations, and complete coping reaction lists for all FMs.

sources.apa_citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers.
Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36.
Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc.
Längle, A. (1992). What Are We Looking for When We Search for Meaning?. Ultimate Reality and Meaning, 15(4), 306–314.

EA_Goal.description: The goal of Existential Analysis is to help a person find a way of living where they can give inner consent to their actions and existence.
EA_Goal.quote: to help man to find a way of living where he can give his inner consent to his own actions.

Motivational_Process_Steps.process_name: Personal Existential Act (PEA) / Steps to Inner Consent
Motivational_Process_Steps.description: The three-step process of motivation and personal decision-making.

steps.quote: Recognizing something in its worth or value, insofar as it speaks to us... Perceiving the sense appeal and value of things...

Bringing the perceived value, challenge or meaning into accordance with one’s inner reality, i.e., examining the consistency with the rest of our values, with attitudes, abilities and capabilities and with our conscience.
The final step in the development of motivation is the inner consent to one’s own active involvement. This consent leads to the presence of the inner person in one's actions.

Phenomenological_Approach.description: The attitude of setting aside all judgements and theories ('epoché') to view facts and phenomena as they show themselves, which is central to finding the essence of the person: their free will.

fundamental_motivations.fundamental_reality: Facts, Reality, Conditions, Truth, Space, Time
fundamental_motivations.negative_pathology_result_general: Anxiety, Phobia, Fear of existence, Psychosis (in the extreme)

detailed_codes.name: Orientation to Facts / Ground to Hold

definition.quote: Meaning is unconditionally realistic. The person living meaningfully will face and grasp the facts. He needs their ground to hold and support him...

inclusion_criteria.text: References to grasping facts, reality testing, or needing ground/support from facts.

detailed_codes.name: Conditions for Being: Protection, Space, Support

definition.quote: This demands three things: protection, space and support.

existential_needs_details: Space ('Do I have enough space for being there?')
Support ('Where do I find support in my life?')

indicators.text: References to fundamental trust in world/self arising from secured protection, space, support.

definition.quote: My active part in this fundamental condition of being here is to accept the positive and endure the negative.

indicators.text: Mentions of accepting conditions, occupying space, relying on support, trusting protection; enduring the difficult/unalterable.
Consequences of unmet conditions: restlessness, insecurity, fear.

fundamental_motivations.core_question: I live - Do I like my life?
fundamental_motivations.negative_pathology_result_general: Depression, Loss of self-worth, Loss of contact (e.g., Borderline, Narcissistic traits)

fundamental_motivations.fundamental_reality: Own Self, Justification, Justice, Respect, Conscience
fundamental_motivations.core_question: I am myself - May I be so?
fundamental_motivations.negative_pathology_result_general: Hysteria, Shame, Low self-esteem, Guilt, Personality disorders (e.g., Narcissistic)

fundamental_motivations.fundamental_reality: Meaning, Goal, Purpose, Future, Value to be realized
fundamental_motivations.core_question: I am here - What am I needed for?
fundamental_motivations.existential_need: Meaning, Goal, Purpose, Future, A Field of Activity
fundamental_motivations.negative_pathology_result_general: Feeling of Emptiness (Existential Vacuum), Frustration, Despair, Addiction, Nihilism

coping_reactions_failure.freezing_paralysis: Fatalism, Loss of Interest, Apathy, Nihilism
